title: Great God! to Me the Sight Afford
description: Great God! to Me the Sight Afford in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 249.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great God! to me the sight af-ford To him of old al-lowed; And let my faith be-hold its Lord De-scend-ing in a cloud.

lines: Great God! to me the sight afford
And let my faith behold its Lord
In that revealing Spirit come down,
And to my inmost soul make known
Who gav'st my soul to be!
Fountain of being, and of power,
The Lord, the mighty God, thou art;
That name in-spoken to my heart,
Our misery doth for pity call,
An and thou art merciful to all

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
